intro: Entries, tastings and scores: how a baking contest is told, and how to speak of conditions.
p.concursante.consejo: It works for men and women: «el concursante», «la concursante». It comes from «concurso».
p.pastelero.consejo: The feminine is «pastelera». The shop where they work is a «pastelería».
p.catador.consejo: It comes from «catar», to taste carefully. There are also wine, cheese and oil tasters.
p.receta.consejo: The first r is strong: «rre-THE-ta». It is also the paper with the medicine a doctor prescribes.
p.convocar.consejo: You call something for a date: «convocar un concurso». It comes from «con» + «vocar», to call.
p.horno.consejo: The h is silent: «OR-no». A bakery where bread is made is also called a «horno».
p.nata.consejo: You whip it to make «nata montada». In Mexico and elsewhere people say «crema».
p.premio.consejo: You say «ganar un premio» and «dar un premio». The ending «-io» is a diphthong: «PRE-myo».
p.puntuación.consejo: It ends in «-ción», like «atención». It also means the use of commas and full stops in writing.
p.apuntarse.glosa: to sign up, to put one's name down
p.apuntarse.consejo: It always takes «a»: «me apunto a un curso». With «el» they merge: «me apunto al concurso».
p.empate.consejo: It is the noun of the verb «empatar». You say «hay un empate» and «quedar en empate».
p.empatar.consejo: It is regular: «empato», «empatas», «empata». You say «empatar con alguien» or «empatar a puntos».
p.rendirse.consejo: The e becomes i: «me rindo», «se rindió». The first r is strong: «rren-DIR-se».
p.batidora.consejo: It comes from «batir», to beat something to mix it. «Batir huevos», «batir nata».
b1.texto:
**Before.** The organisers **convocan** the contest. Each **concursante** picks a **receta**, buys the ingredients and practises. Whoever wants to take part **se apunta**.

**The day.** The **pastelero** puts on the **delantal** (apron), mixes the dough with the **batidora** and puts the cake in the **horno**. Then the **catadores** taste each cake and give it a **puntuación**.

**Afterwards.** The cake with the most points wins the **premio**. If two cakes have the same points, they **empatan** and there is an **empate**. A contestant can **rendirse** if they cannot go on.

**Conditions.** To talk about what will happen only in certain cases, you use conjunctions with the subjunctive: **a menos que**, **con tal de que**. With **aunque** you can talk about a real fact or about a possibility.
b2.f0.texto: The neighbours' association has called a cake contest.
b2.f1.texto: I have signed up with my grandmother's recipe.
b2.f2.texto: Who is going to taste the cakes?
b2.f3.texto: There will be three tasters, unless one of them drops out.
b2.f4.texto: Although I am nervous, I am not giving up.
b2.f5.texto: The prize for the winner will be a new mixer.
b2.f6.texto: If two cakes tie, the final will be repeated on Saturday.
b2.f7.texto: Then on Saturday I will bring more cream and my best apron.
b3.titulo: From the oven to the table
b4.titulo: Conditions: a menos que and aunque
b4.texto:
**A menos que** (= unless) and **con tal de que** (as long as) talk about a condition and always take the **subjunctive**: **Ganará, a menos que se rinda.** **Puedes entrar con tal de que traigas tu receta.**

**Aunque** changes with what you want to say:

- **Aunque + indicative**: a real fact. **Aunque estoy nerviosa, no me rindo.**
- **Aunque + subjunctive**: you do not know if it will happen, or it does not matter. **Aunque llueva, haremos el concurso.**

**Verbs with a fixed preposition:** **apuntarse a**, **presentarse a**, **encargarse de**. With «el» they merge: **me apunto al concurso**.
b4.e0.texto: Marta's cake will win, unless it burns in the oven.
b4.e1.texto: Even if it rains, the contest will take place in the square.
b4.e2.texto: You can take part as long as you bring your own recipe.
b5.f0.texto: When the ovens went out, the square smelled of burnt sugar and cinnamon.
b5.f1.texto: On the long tables the cakes shone like a field of flowers.
b5.f2.texto: The tasters tried each piece with their eyes closed.
b5.f3.texto: The neighbourhood pastry chef waited beside his oven with his hands white with flour.
b5.f4.texto: In the hall you could only hear the clinking of spoons against plates.
b5.f5.texto: Shortly before midnight, the most experienced taster raised her hand.
b5.f6.texto: A thick silence fell over the hall like a heavy blanket.
b5.f7.texto: In a firm voice she announced that the prize would go to whoever respected the original recipe.
b5.f8.texto: Nobody gave up that night although some contestants ran out of cream.
b5.f9.texto: In the end, two cakes tied on the top score under the yellow light of the bulbs.
b6.o0.refuerzo: It takes the indicative: «porque se rinde».
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «a menos que se rinda». It always takes the subjunctive.
b6.o2.refuerzo: It takes the indicative: «ya que se rinde».
b6.pregunta: Which conjunction always takes the subjunctive?
b7.frase: Ganará la tarta, a menos que se ____.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «a menos que» takes the present subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That is indicative; «a menos que» needs the subjunctive.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That is the future indicative; here you need the subjunctive.
b7.pregunta: Which form does «a menos que» need?
b8.frase: Me he apuntado a un concurso de tartas
b8.traduccion: I have signed up for a cake contest
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Rendirse» is to stop competing, not to have the same points.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Convocar» is to call a contest or a meeting.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: «empatar» is to finish with the same points.
b9.pregunta: What do two cakes with the same points do?
b11.o1.refuerzo: Yes: a + el = al. «Me apunto al concurso».
b12.o0: Aunque estoy nerviosa, no me rindo
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: with the indicative you speak of a fact you already know.
b12.o1: Aunque esté nerviosa, no me rendiré
b12.o1.refuerzo: With the subjunctive you speak of something possible or that does not matter.
b12.o2.refuerzo: With the subjunctive you do not know whether it will rain.
b12.pregunta: Which sentence speaks of a real fact?
p.convocado.consejo: From «convocar», to call people together; the «v» sounds like «b».
p.tartas.consejo: Plural of «tarta»; the stress is on «TAR».
p.apuntado.consejo: Past participle of «apuntarse», to sign up; «apuntar» also means to note down.
p.catadores.consejo: From «catar», to taste; the «c» before «a» sounds like «k».
p.alguno.consejo: «Alguno» becomes «algún» before a masculine noun, as in «algún día».
p.retire.consejo: Subjunctive of «retirarse» after «que», for a possible event.
p.rindo.consejo: From «rendirse», to give up; «rindo» is the form for «yo».
p.ganadora.consejo: Feminine form of «ganador», the one who wins.
p.empatan.consejo: From «empatar»; the noun «empate» means a tie.
p.repetirá.consejo: Future tense of «repetir», third person: the «á» marks the future.
p.traeré.consejo: Future of «traer» for «yo»: the «é» marks the future.
p.delantal.consejo: It comes from «delante», in front: you wear it on the front.
p.ganará.consejo: Future of «ganar», third person: the «á» marks the future.
p.queme.consejo: Subjunctive of «quemar» after «que», for a possible event.
p.celebrará.consejo: Future of «celebrar»: it means to hold an event or to celebrate.
p.apagaron.consejo: Third person plural of «apagar» in the past: the opposite of «encender».
p.brillaban.consejo: Imperfect of «brillar»: an action that went on in the past.
p.probaban.consejo: Imperfect of «probar»: «-aban» is the ending for «ellos» with -ar verbs.
p.oía.consejo: The accent on «í» breaks the diphthong: it has two syllables, o-I-a.
p.contra.consejo: «Contra» means against; it can also be a noun: the drawback.
p.medianoche.consejo: «Medianoche» joins «media» and «noche»: the middle of the night.
p.catadora.consejo: Feminine of «catador», from the verb «catar», to taste.
p.veterana.consejo: Feminine of «veterano»: someone with a long experience in something.
p.denso.consejo: «Denso» describes something compact, like a thick fog.
p.cayó.consejo: Past tense of «caer», third person: the «ó» takes the stress.
p.respetara.consejo: Subjunctive after «quien» for an imagined person: whoever respected.
p.original.consejo: The «g» before «i» sounds like «h», and the stress falls on «NAL».
p.rindió.consejo: Third person of «rendirse» in the past: someone stopped fighting.
p.concursantes.consejo: Plural of «concursante», a person who takes part in a contest.
p.empataron.consejo: Third person plural in the past of «empatar», to draw or tie.
p.bombillas.consejo: «Bombilla» is a light bulb; the «ll» sounds like «y».
